editorial.marketOverview: Nasdaq/QQQ remains bearish with elevated downside risk after Thursday's broad selloff, weak semiconductor leadership, poor breadth and high VIX. Asian AI-chip weakness reinforces risk aversion but does not yet prove Friday US cash-market follow-through.
editorial.whatChanged: WSJ reported both US Treasury yields during Asian trading, allowing a correctly scaled +28.20 bp curve from 5.0089% 10Y and 4.7269% 2Y. This supersedes the stale +25.4 bp reading but does not alter the directional assessment. No new independent Open Watch catalyst.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Falling yields reflect some flight-to-quality demand and are not automatically bullish for growth stocks when equity risk appetite is deteriorating. Fed tightening expectations appear in market reporting, but direct current FedWatch probabilities are unavailable and not invented.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 20: failed-rebound and downside-continuation risk remains elevated until US QQQ/SOX breadth and volatility establish a reversal. Monday November 23: assess follow-through versus stabilization. Tuesday November 24: reassess rates, AI leadership and earnings reactions. These are conditional paths, not predicted daily returns.
editorial.bullCase: Sustained QQQ relative strength versus SPY, renewed SOX/SMH leadership, improving breadth, easing VXN/VIX and stable-to-lower yields could invalidate the bearish baseline; a sharp relief rally remains possible after oversold conditions.
editorial.bearCase: Continued AI financing and valuation worries, semiconductor underperformance, elevated volatility and weak breadth could extend selling across Friday, Monday and Tuesday. Overnight Asian declines amplify risk but are not direct US cash confirmation.
editorial.watchNext: Friday Michigan final consumer sentiment and inflation expectations 10:00 EST; synchronized QQQ/SPY, SOX/SMH, breadth and volatility; official Treasury yields, direct FedWatch, Brent/WTI matching contracts; Monday confirmation and Tuesday earnings timing checks.
